question.leadin: Name some World War II leaders.
question.text: This leader coined the term "iron curtain" to describe a barrier between western and eastern Europe and gave his famous "this was their finest hour" speech prior to the Battle of Britain.
question.clue: Clement Attlee replaced this man at the Potsdam Conference after the Conservatives were voted out in July 1945.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about Brexit.
swap.text: This Conservative prime minister resigned as a result of Brexit. Theresa May succeeded him in July 2016.
swap.clue: In August 2011, this leader controversially proposed that social media might be restricted during riots, such as the ones which swept his capital earlier that month.

question.text: Earlier, this ruler successfully repelled a Viking invasion of England. He is the only English ruler with the epithet "The Great."
question.clue: A daughter of this ruler extended a defense system in which thirty fortresses were garrisoned by four men to each wall perch; that system of burhs was detailed in the Burghal Hidage during the reign of this ruler's son, Edward the Elder.

swap.leadin: This ruler defeated Saladin at the Battles of Arsuf and Jaffa during the Third Crusade.
swap.text: Identify this English king who would later be held for ransom by the Holy Roman Emperor Henry VI. Only spending six months of his reign in England, he would die besieging the French castle of Chalus.
swap.answerHtml: Richard I of England [accept Richard the Lionheart; prompt on “Richard”]
swap.clue: He was later captured by Leopold of Austria and ransomed.

question.text: The Williamite War began after this 1688 event that resulted in the passage of the English Bill of Rights. A letter from the "Immortal Seven" sparked this event in which William and Mary took the English throne.
question.clue: This event targeted a ruler who had been forced to put down Monmouth's Rebellion near the start of his reign.

swap.leadin: This man's life story was recounted in a lengthy poem by Blind Harry.
swap.text: Identify this iconic Scottish hero and fighter for independence, the victor at the Battle of Stirling Bridge.
swap.clue: This man resigned as Guardian after losing a battle where his army was arranged in sheltrons.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the history of internet development.
question.text: Packet switching was pioneered in this country after Donald Davies developed the NPL network. Early computer scientists in this country cracked the Enigma machine.
question.clue: The past is constantly progressing towards greatness according to a school of thought named after a political party in this country.

swap.leadin: This man banished all Jews from England in the 1290 Edict of Expulsion.
swap.text: Name this English king, whose nickname refers to his above average height. Before he acceded to the throne, he defeated an alliance of barons who revolted against his father, Henry III.
swap.clue: He employed James of St. George to build an "Iron Ring" that included Flint and Rhuddlan.

question.text: This member of the earlier Hohenstaufen family succeeded Frederick Barbarossa and gained control of Sicily by marrying Constance I. An English king of this name and number founded Eton College and faced Jack Cade's Revolt.
question.clue: This king was deposed and fled to Scotland following the Battle of Towton.

swap.leadin: This man gained power after leading a coup against Roger Mortimer, whom he killed at Nottingham Castle with the help of the Earl of Salisbury.
swap.text: Name this king, who ruled during England's victories at Crecy and Neville's Cross as well as the opening of the Good Parliament.
swap.clue: Under this king, the Statute of Laborers was introduced as an attempt to keep wages low despite major population loss caused by the Black Death.

question.text: This British adventurer detailed his Hajj in The Pilgrimage to Al-Medinah and Meccah, translated The Arabian Nights and, with John Speke, searched for the source of the .
question.clue: This man. He led a tumultuous expedition to the large lakes of southern Africa with John Hanning Speke.

swap.leadin: During this man's term, George Soros worked over his country's financial system and forced him to withdraw from the Exchange Rate Mechanism on "Black Wednesday."
swap.text: Name this Conservative British PM of the 1990s who fashioned the "Back to Basics" campaign. He won the so-called "Soap Box election" after he went to the streets and literally stood on soapboxes to deliver his message.
swap.clue: This politician signed the Downing Street Declaration with Albert Reynolds.

question.leadin: The Protestant Reformation reached all across Europe and affected nearly every Kingdom. answer the following questions about some of the major participants.
question.text: Martin Bucer chose exile in this kingdom after he continued to resist Emperor Charles V's enforcement of Catholic rites and dogmas in his native Strasbourg; this kingdom famously dissolved all of its monasteries after its legislature passed the Act of Supremacy.
question.answerHtml: The Kingdom of England [prompt on Britain by saying “Which part of Britain?”]
question.clue: In the mid-14th century, this kingdom's Company of the Staple was granted a monopoly on the trade of its primary export.

swap.leadin: Newgate Prison was mostly destroyed during this event.
swap.text: Name this violent anti-Catholic uprising which broke out in London in response to the Papists Act of 1778.
swap.clue: Participants wore blue ribbons in their hats in imitation of its initiator, who was defended in court by Thomas Erskine and acquitted.

question.leadin: In Nennius's History of the Britons, a fight between two of these creatures serves as a metaphor for Celtic resistance to the Saxon invasion.
question.text: Name this creature depicted on Henry Tudor's banners at the Battle of Bosworth Field as a reference to the 7th-century king of Gwynedd Cadwaladr ap Cadwallon ("GWIN-eth cad-WA-la-der ap cad-WA-lon").
question.answerHtml: Welsh dragon [or ddraig Cymraeg (“thraig cum-raig”); or ddraig goch (“goh”); accept red dragon; accept white dragon; accept ddraig gwyn]

swap.leadin: Description acceptable. Stale sandwiches provided by one service were a common talking point supporting this policy, which led to the creation of companies like Connex.
swap.text: Identify or describe this policy in John Major's 1992 platform, which critics claim reduced safety standards and led to accidents at Southall, Ladbroke Grove, and Hatfield.
swap.answerHtml: privatization of British Rail [accept answers involving turning over public rail infrastructure to private owners or companies]

question.text: On the recapture of South Georgia, Margaret Thatcher jingoistically told reporters to "congratulate our armed forces and the Marines" and to do this action. Ted Heath is said to have sardonically repeated this word after Thatcher resigned.
question.answerHtml: “rejoice” [or word forms such as rejoicing; accept “just rejoice at that news and congratulate our forces and the Marines”; accept “rejoice, rejoice”; accept “rejoice, rejoice, rejoice”]

swap.leadin: This man entered Parliament in 1717 as the representative for Seaford.
swap.text: Name this man who served as prime minister for 11 years before dying in 1754, at which point his brother, the Duke of Newcastle, succeeded him.

question.text: Letitia Ann Sage became the first British woman to fly at Vicenzo Lunardi's 1785 ballooning exhibition at this London area. A crowd protesting John Wilkes's imprisonment were fired on by troops in a 1768 massacre in this area.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about history, punctuation and the history of punctuation.
swap.text: This author was the first to suggest to Gibbon that his endnotes in Decline and Fall be published as footnotes. He published a history of England during the years from 1754 to 1761.
